<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro secúndo Machabæórum
<r>2 Mac 7:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Cóntigit autem et septem fratres una cum matre sua apprehénsos compélli a rege édere contra fas carnes porcínas, flagris et táureis cruciátos.
<n>2</n> Unus autem ex illis, qui erat primus, sic ait: Quid quæris et quid vis díscere a nobis? Paráti sumus mori, magis quam pátrias Dei leges prævaricári.
<n>3</n> Irátus ítaque rex iussit sartágines et ollas ǽneas succéndi. Quibus statim succénsis,
<n>4</n> Iussit ei qui prior fúerat locútus, amputári linguam, et, cute cápitis abstrácta, summas quoque manus et pedes ei præscíndi, céteris eius frátribus et matre inspiciéntibus.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Congregáti sunt inimíci nostri, et gloriántur in virtúte sua: cóntere fortitúdinem illórum, Dómine, et dispérge illos:
* Ut cognóscant quia non est álius qui pugnet pro nobis, nisi tu, Deus noster.
<r>℣.</r> Dispérge illos in virtúte tua, et déstrue eos, protéctor noster, Dómine.
<r>℟.</r> Ut cognóscant quia non est álius qui pugnet pro nobis, nisi tu, Deus noster.
b.a3e67bbf65:

<r>Benediction.</r> May God the Father Omnipotent, be to us merciful and clement.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the second book of Machabees
<r>2 Mac 7:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> It came to pass also, that seven brethren, together with their mother, were apprehended, and compelled by the king to eat swine's flesh against the law, for which end they were tormented with whips and scourges.
<n>2</n> But one of them, who was the eldest, said thus: What wouldst thou ask, or learn of us? we are ready to die rather than to transgress the laws of God, received from our fathers.
<n>3</n> Then the king being angry commanded fryingpans, and brazen caldrons to be made hot: which forthwith being heated,
<n>4</n> He commanded to cut out the tongue of him that had spoken first: and the skin of his head being drawn off, to chop off also the extremities of his hands and feet, the rest of his brethren, and his mother, looking on.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Our enemies are gathered together, and make their boast of their own strength. O Lord, break their power, and scatter them
* That they may know that there is none other that fighteth for us, but only Thou, O our God!
<r>℣.</r> Scatter them in thy strength, and destroy them, O Lord our Shield.
<r>℟.</r> That they may know that there is none other that fighteth for us, but only Thou, O our God!

<n>6</n> Dicéntes: Dóminus Deus aspíciet veritátem, et consolábitur in nobis, quemádmodum in protestatióne cántici declarávit Móyses: Et in servis suis consolábitur.

b.1c3fd2858a:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>exto Kaléndas Novémbris Luna vicésima séptima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>V</h>igília sanctórum Apostolórum Simónis et Iudæ.
<h>A</h>bulæ, in Hispánia, pássio sanctórum Vincéntii, Sabínæ et Christétæ. Hi primum in equúleo ádeo sunt exténti, ut omnes membrórum compáges laxaréntur; deínde cápita eórum, lapídibus superpósita, usque ad cérebri excussiónem válidis véctibus sunt contúsa, atque ita ipsi martýrium complevérunt, sub Prǽside Daciáno.
<h>A</h>pud castrum Tyle, in Gállia, sancti Floréntii Mártyris.
<h>I</h>n Cappadócia sanctárum Mártyrum Capitolínæ, eiúsque ancíllæ Erothéidis, quæ sub Diocletiáno sunt passæ.
<h>A</h>pud Indos sancti Fruméntii Epíscopi, qui, primum ibi captívus, deínde, Epíscopus a sancto Athanásio ordinátus, Evangélium in ea província propagávit.
<h>N</h>eápoli, in Campánia, sancti Gaudiósi, Epíscopi Africáni, qui ob Wandalórum persecutiónem venit in Campániam, et, in monastério apud eam urbem, sancto fine quiévit.
<h>I</h>n Æthiópia sancti Elésbaan Regis, qui, Christi hóstibus expugnátis, ac, témpore Iustíni Imperatóris, misso regio diadémate Hierosólymam, monásticam vitam, ut vóverat, agens, migrávit ad Dóminum.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.e0b473c05f:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 27th 2027, the 27th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>he morrow is the eve of the holy Apostles Simon and Jude.
<h>U</h>pon the same 27th day of October, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Avila, in Spain, the holy martyrs Vincent, Sabina, and Christeta, who were first racked until all their joints were loosened, then stones were put upon their heads which were beaten with heavy logs of wood, until their brains were burst, and so they finished their testimony under the (Emperor Diocletian and the) President Dacian.
<h>A</h>t Thil-Chateau, (in Burgundy, in the third century,) the holy martyr Florence.
<h>I</h>n Cappadocia, the holy martyrs Capitolina and Erotheis her handmaiden, who suffered under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>I</h>n Ethiopia, holy Frumentius, first Bishop of that country, who was first a captive there, then was ordained Bishop by holy Athanasius, and spread the Gospel in that country.
<h>A</h>t Naples, holy Gaudiosus, Bishop (of Abitina,) in Africa, who came to Campagna on account of the persecution by the Vandals, and died an holy death in a monastery in the city above named.
<h>L</h>ikewise in Ethiopia, the holy King Elesbaan, who, after he had overcome the enemies of Christ in the time of the Emperor Justin, sent his kingly crown to Jerusalem, and made himself a monk in fulfilment of a vow, and so lived until he passed away hence to be ever with the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
